analysis: release-swift.yml: the reviewer-approval `environment:` binding is removed from build-and-release, stage-release and publish-release. It is replaced by a `verify-source` step (scripts/provider-release-resume.py) in resolve-env that checks out master, and every downstream job checks out `workflow_sha`. The header comment explicitly assumes trusted repository writers. The publication artifact is now fetched by artifact ID and digest with payload and provenance SHA-256 values passed through (a positive integrity improvement). The keychain handling is hardened, and BINARY_HASH and related values are now written to GITHUB_ENV in one block. The qualification-request flow is dropped; the release endpoint is described as registering the exact build before publication. Risk: A-005, A-011 and A-017 depend on the release path being separate from App Attest qualification (T-054). The registration code (the publication script and coordinator release handler) was not supplied, so the integration pass should verify that CI registration cannot qualify builds and that verify-source cannot be bypassed by a workflow_dispatch from a non-master ref. ci.yml has only test-step additions and no secrets; no security issue was seen there.

findings.detail: The `environment:` binding is removed from build-and-release, stage-release and publish-release. Previously production tags had to pass the environment's deployment protection rules before the Developer ID signing identity, the R2 keys and the coordinator release key (A-005) were released. Now `verify-source` in resolve-env is the only gate, and the new header comment says release jobs need no approvals and that the design assumes trusted repository writers. Any actor who can push a tag or dispatch a workflow from a branch, or who compromises a writer account, would no longer be stopped by a human approval step. The jobs hold the secrets that drive the binary-hash registry (A-011) and release registration. The old approval step was a second factor; the new check relies on one script on master and on the workflow file of the triggering ref. Fix: keep environment protection (required reviewers and branch/tag restrictions) on the credential-consuming jobs, or add an equivalent mandatory control outside the workflow, such as repository rulesets that protect tags and the workflow files. Also add this change to the threat model.
findings.title: Release jobs drop GitHub environment approval gates, leaving a source check as the only guard on signing and registry credentials

findings.detail: The summary text previously said the release key cannot approve builds, that qualification evidence goes to the admin app-attest builds endpoint, and that qualification stays an independent operator step. The head text now says the release endpoint validates and registers the exact official build before publication, and the job is renamed 'Register and publish exact signed release'. The qualification-request.json output is removed. The registration logic itself is not in this diff. If the CI release key's registration now creates or implies durable App Attest build qualification, T-054 and A-017 are weakened: a CI-key compromise or a malicious workflow run would be enough to make a build servable. Fix: confirm that release registration cannot create a durable qualification or approve a CDHash. Keep the qualification step separate and operator-authenticated. Update the threat model and the A-017/T-054 text to match the new flow.
findings.title: Publish flow now registers the signed build through the release endpoint, which may bypass the independent build-qualification step
